title: Copilot Studio: conversational set-up of connector connections with in-chat sign-in
summary: Hold: the PowerShell reference explicitly documents Blocked as the connector classification, contrary to the briefing's statement that this value is not shown. The admin path also omits the connector's three-dot menu, which is where the Block action is located. The roadmap facts and the related connection-management behaviour are supported.

claims.claim: The Connection Required card offers Set up connection, Retry and Deny.
claims.quote: Set up connection ... Retry ... Deny

claims.claim: Users connect each item required by the action and then return to chat.

claims.quote: Some tools in a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent sign in with each user's own account instead of one shared account. Before the agent can use one of these tools for you, you need to connect your account.

claims.claim: Manage your connections lists tools, flows and AI models using the user's own account.
claims.quote: The Manage your connections page lists the tools, flows, and AI models in the agent that use your own account.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Connections are saved per channel, and users of the same agent in several channels set up connections in each.
claims.quote: Connections are saved for each agent and each channel. If you chat with the same agent in more than one channel, set up your connections in each channel.

claims.claim: In Microsoft Teams, the agent retries the action automatically after the user connects.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Teams, the agent retries the action automatically after you connect.

claims.claim: Deny cancels the action and the agent does not retry it.
claims.quote: Cancels the action. The agent doesn't try the action again and tells you that it was canceled.

claims.claim: The Create or pick connections dialog lets the user select an existing connection or create one.
claims.quote: In the Create or pick connections dialog, for each service under Name, select an existing connection under Connection, or create a new one.

claims.claim: The user's selected account and connection determine the identity under which the agent acts through these tools.
claims.quote: Some tools in a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent sign in with each user's own account instead of one shared account. ... You can remove a connection from the agent when you no longer want the agent to act with your account.

claims.claim: Users can remove their connections with Disconnect, and that removal cannot be undone.
claims.quote: Above the list, select Disconnect. ... The connections are removed for this agent in the channel where you chat with it, such as Microsoft Teams. You can't undo this action.

claims.where: Why it matters; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A tool blocked by a data policy cannot be selected by the maker.
claims.quote: When a data policy blocks a tool, the tool appears unavailable in the Add a tool panel and you can't select it.

claims.claim: Publishing or running an agent that uses a data-policy-blocked tool can fail.
claims.quote: The message explains that your organization's data policy blocks the tool, so the tool can't be used, even by an agent, and publishing or running an agent that uses it can fail.

claims.claim: Data policies can prevent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.claim: A data policy applies to Copilot Studio agents in the environments in its scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.claim: Configuring the policy is an administrator operation requiring administrative rights for its scope.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure Copilot Studio and Power Platform data policies in the Power Platform admin center. ... Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: An existing data policy is changed using Edit Policy rather than New Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing data policy, select the data policy and select Edit Policy.

claims.claim: The blocking path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Next > connector > Block.
claims.quote: Use the search box to find the connector you want. ... Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then: ... To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select Block.
claims.fix: Insert the documented connector menu step in controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table: 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Next > connector > three dots > Block'. The cited page places Block inside that menu, not directly on the connector.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-id> -Classification <group> -Connectors <connector-list> classifies connectors in a DLP policy group.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... The Add-ConnectorsToPolicy takes the connectors as a list of objects and adds them to the specified group of the given DLP policy.

claims.claim: The cited PowerShell reference does not show the classification value that means Blocked.
claims.quote: The name of the group to which the connectors should be added. Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).
claims.fix: Replace 'The page read for this briefing does not show the value that means Blocked, so check the reference before scripting.' with 'Use -Classification Blocked to put the connectors in the Blocked group.'

claims.claim: Manage your connections is a user-side connection-management page, not an administrator control.
